title: Morphisms, semistability and stable modifications of multipointed curves
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $P=(C,D)$ and $Q$ be multipointed $T$-curves [def-trf-multipointed-curve]: $p:C\to T$ and $d:D\to T$ are the curve and marking structure maps and $i:D\hookrightarrow C$ the marking closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $p\circ i=d$. Empty markings and nonproper, nonseparated curves are allowed. A morphism $f:P\to Q$ is a pair of $T$-morphisms $f_C,f_D$ commuting with the markings. The canonical base changes of these maps and of the marking are given by the fibre-product universal property. The pair is semistable if every point of each geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] of $p$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] or an ordinary double point (the completed local-ring condition of [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data]), $d$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and the marking lies in the relative smooth locus of $p$. For a specified morphism $\eta:S\to T$ (in applications the generic point of integral $T$), $f$ is an $\eta$-modification if both maps are proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], each is an isomorphism over some open $U$ [def-weil-open-immersion] for which both $U$ and its inverse image are schematically dense, and both maps become isomorphisms after base change to $S$. Schematic density of an open $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ means injectivity of $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$, equivalently injectivity on sections on every open of $Z$. The special points of a geometric curve fibre are the union of the geometric marking and the nonsmooth points. Such an $\eta$-modification is stable if its source is semistable and there is no irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of any geometric curve fibre, isomorphic over its algebraically closed ground field $\Omega$ to the projective line $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], whose image under the geometric fibre map is a singleton and whose intersection with the special points has cardinality at most two. A projective-line component is encoded by a closed immersion of $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$ into the fibre over $\Omega$, with image an irreducible component.

source.place: Temkin, Stable modification of relative curves, §1.2 (printed p. 2), §4 preamble and Remark 4.1 (printed pp. 24--25). Primary PDF: https://math.huji.ac.il/~temkin/papers/Stable_Modification.pdf
